chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Sulayman, from Marwak ibn Ubayd, from Nashit ibn Salih, who said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'I do not see any harm in eating the bustard, and it is good for hemorrhoids and back pain, and it is among what aids in frequent intercourse.'

key_terms.الْحُبَارَى: Bustard, a type of large ground-dwelling bird

ai.seo_question: What are you looking for rulings on eating specific birds in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Hasan al-Askeri (peace be upon him) affirms the permissibility of the bustard bird (*al-hubara*), highlighting its therapeutic properties for hemorrhoids and back pain as well as its aphrodisiac qualities. This reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of integrating practical medical wisdom with jurisprudential rulings, where the Prophet and Imams often provided specific dietary advice for health maintenance.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Suleyman, from Marwak Bin Ubeyd, from Basheyt Bin Salih who said,

‘I heard Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 1st saying: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> do not see a problem with eating the bustard, and it is very good for the hemorrhoids, and the back pain, and it is from what aids upon the frequency of the copulation’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn Sulayman from Marwak ibn ‘Ubayd from Nashit ibn Salih who has said the following: “I once heard abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘It is not unlawful to eat the meat of al- Habara ’ (bustard). It is good for hemorrhoids and back-pain and it helps increase the ability to go to bed with one’s wife.’”
